environment_note: pandas/statsmodels wheels are blocked by a Windows application-control policy in this environment (DLL load failure, verified by reinstalling pandas 3.1.1 and 2.3.3); scripts use csv + numpy + scipy instead, same estimators implemented directly.

role_sources.unit: data/README.md 'Panel structure': numeric state IDs 1-39, one row per state-year
role_sources.outcome: data/README.md and plan.md: cigsale = per-capita cigarette SALES in packs, not consumption
role_sources.treatment_group: data/README.md: california is True for state 3 only, all 31 years; AGENTS.md: treatment = california AND year >= 1989
role_sources.time_indicator: after_treatment is a year dummy (year >= 1989) for every state - used only to CHECK the post period, never as the treatment (README rule 2)
role_sources.covariate: plan.md test 1 says no covariates; README caveat 3 documents lnincome/beer/age15to24 missing in many years (beer missing 1970-1983 and 1998-2000, age15to24 missing 1991-2000, lnincome missing 1970-1971 and 1998-2000), so adding any would drop rows

checks.treatment_not_after_treatment: after_treatment is True in 456 post-1988 rows that are NOT California; it fails the check 'zero for control units' and is not used as treatment
checks.staggered_timing: no - the single treated unit starts in 1989, so plain two-way fixed effects is the planned specification
